title: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Eighth edition, Volume 6, Burning glasses-Climate - EB.16
text: The reader has no doubt remarked the analogy between the chemical relations of antimony and arsenic and those of phosphorus. Indeed, no two element are anomalous in this respect as arsenic and phosphorus, save that one is metallic. For other not. There is a resemblance, however, even in physical properties for the colour of phosphorus closely resembles that of arsenic. These three deterrents, in spite of one being non-metallic, form a group distinguished by forming oxides with 3 and 6 esp. of oxygen, and gaseous compounds of a field odor with 6 esp of hydrogen.
